sharedFoundation: XTDB writes shared by the Datalog and native query surfaces

measurement.meaning: Driver dispatch-to-settlement wall spans; COMMIT SYNC remains composite. No independent engine CPU, wire execution or indexing instant was observed.
measurement.limits: One 1k sparse FACT-subject scope and one 30s diagnostic. No configured-entity/full-scale coverage, sustainable-rate calibration, comparative promotion, host-idleness or Rust case. Earlier co-run failures remain unchanged.

owningSource.mechanism: Each retraction reads getById for reserved-write validation and transaction change capture before calling adapter.retract
queryRows captures sourceK, applies original scope/id/recorded/retirement predicates, and then recomputes pending row overlays
retract performs a second independent queryRows by id; getById at line546 invokes the same source lookup
Existing persisted assertion document key is JSON.stringify([scopeKey,row.id]); this supports a separate native-key predicate hypothesis without a second store
Per-adapter transaction state owns sourceK, pending rows, claims and nested savepoint state; no shared committed identity cache exists

hypotheses.mechanism: Keep getById's current backend read. Retain one private immutable copy of that result (or miss) in the active transaction; let the immediately matching retract consume it once if the same transaction/sourceK/id and unchanged pending row snapshot still prove equivalence. Any failed eligibility check uses the original queryRows path.
changes: Private TransactionState handoff and XTDB adapter implementation only; no user schema, query DSL, public API or driver protocol change
Maximum one handoff entry and64KiB of scalar payload per transaction state; oversize/non-flat values bypass reuse
Private cached rows contain only copied primitive assertion columns. Returned objects retain their current behavior; their mutation cannot corrupt the private handoff
Compare the pending-row snapshot field by field with Object.is, including in-place mutation and signed zero. A changed or newly inserted/retracted pending row invalidates reuse
Nested child states and every retry start with an empty handoff; failed/successful children do not leak it into the parent. No cache survives transaction completion
Only the same scope/generation-bound adapter state and sourceK qualify. Outside-transaction, history, basis-qualified and arbitrary query reads stay on the original route
Do not alter reserved-write authorization, command claims, source-position CAS, conflict/replay-safety or unknown-ACK reconciliation
hypotheses.prediction: Ten unchanged target retractions require10 committed identity SELECT callbacks instead of20, while original source-basis/claim/submit/receipt/visibility calls and returned rows remain equivalent
hypotheses.retirementAndConcurrentWrites: A captured source result may only be reused for internal mutation at that same sourceK; public getById still executes its normal read. Own pending changes invalidate the handoff. A foreign commit must still produce the existing source-CAS conflict and an explicitly replay-safe retry must reacquire sourceK and an empty handoff. Test this interleaving instead of assuming raw retirement metadata is immutable.
hypotheses.failurePolicy: Any uncertainty, unsupported row shape, id mismatch, child-state crossing, changed overlay, payload cap or incomplete lookup falls back to the existing lookup. Correctness and uncertainty tests precede any timed trial.

hypotheses.mechanism: For the existing id-specific source lookup, add parameterized _id=JSON.stringify([scopeKey,id]) while retaining original scope/id/recorded/retirement predicates, projection, decoder and pending overlay. No row-layout or write change.
hypotheses.prediction: Identity callback count stays20, but per-lookup driver wall time may fall if the pinned native planner uses its document identity path. That planner benefit is a hypothesis, not an established fact.
gates: Verify the admitted source writer always supplies this exact key, including correction replacement, scope/generation separation, unusual Unicode/id spellings and reopened stores
Refuse or fall back for source mappings whose native-key completeness is not established; never silently omit a legacy or externally authored row
Retain original half-open/recorded/source cuts and mutable pending overlays; compare all identities and retirement metadata with the unchanged reference
Measure observed SQL shape, callback count, public ACK and per-lookup wall spans rather than treating key syntax as proof of an optimization

hypotheses.mechanism: The core already owns the validated transaction operations, so it could invoke an optional internal adapter prefetch SPI inside the same transaction to fetch only the known retraction target IDs in bounded chunks at sourceK. Subsequent reads still recompute current pending overlays.
hypotheses.prediction: Ten targets can use one bounded source identity query rather than10 or20, without loading the whole store or changing the user transaction API
hypotheses.additionalCost: Requires separately justified shared internal SPI/core integration and cross-backend fallback tests. The XTDB adapter cannot infer all future target IDs from an arbitrary Effect callback; do not invent a batch from expected answers or evaluate facts in the host.
gates: Bound IDs, payload, chunk width and map lifetime; preserve absent IDs, duplicates, command order and sourceK across every chunk
Keep pending inserts/retractions, required/reserved authorization and transaction change records identical to the existing sequential path
Retain independent nested/parallel transaction, foreign scope/generation, retirement, retry, cancellation and unknown-ACK controls

timedPilotContract.control: Freeze a fresh unmodified control before the first product edit; the isolated observed run is measured attribution, not a three-repeat promotion control
timedPilotContract.numericProfile: Same1k sparse subject fixture,256logical clients,480offers at16/s,dispatch16,pending4096,30swindow,30sscheduled-offer deadline,6ten-entity corrections at0.2/s,896MiB1CPU client plus existing3GiB XTDB and2GiB Q reservations
timedPilotContract.sourceAndEvidence: Separate named source/build/fixture/oracle/profile identities and exact driver callbacks; fresh scopes; no query deadline, write semantics, staleness or resource-cap relaxation
timedPilotContract.decision: Correctness or unresolved lifecycle failure rejects the candidate. Any availability/liveness failure remains failed. A small gate can validate the predicted call-count mechanism; performance promotion still needs actual common-path capacity controls, adequate samples and matched repeats.
